entry.title: Plage du Verger, Cancale
entry.summary: Plage du Verger is a wide beach of fine sand at Cancale in Brittany, on the shore of the Bay of Mont-Saint-Michel. The sea goes out far at low tide and returns quickly, so timing matters.

entry.title: Plage de Coz Pors, Tregastel
entry.summary: Plage de Coz Pors is a sheltered sandy beach in Tregastel on the Pink Granite Coast of Brittany, with rounded pink rocks, small islands offshore and clear water. At low tide the sand spreads out, and at high tide the beach becomes small.

entry.title: Espiguette Beach, Le Grau-du-Roi
entry.summary: Espiguette is a wide, wild beach of fine sand at the southern tip of the Camargue near Le Grau-du-Roi, with dunes, a lighthouse and a very long shoreline. Parts of it are protected, and the sea is shallow and gentle with a long sandbar.

entry.title: Plage Saint-Francoise, Ajaccio
entry.summary: Plage Saint-Francoise is a small town beach in Ajaccio, Corsica, a strip of sand and pebbles with clear blue water and mountains rising behind the bay. The old citadel is close, and the centre of town is a short walk away.

entry.title: Plage de Morgat, Crozon
entry.summary: Morgat is a seaside village on the Crozon peninsula in Brittany, with a wide sheltered beach of fine sand, a harbour and a promenade of old seafront houses. The bay is calm, and boats leave from the harbour for the sea caves along the coast.

entry.title: Praia do Tamariz, Estoril
entry.summary: Praia do Tamariz is the main beach of Estoril on the Lisbon coast, a curve of golden sand sheltered by a breakwater, with the casino gardens and a seafront promenade behind. The water is calmer than at most Atlantic beaches, and the train from Lisbon stops nearby.

entry.title: Praia do Algodio, Ericeira
entry.summary: Praia do Algodio is a small sand and rock beach on the coast of Ericeira, a white surf village north-west of Lisbon. The Atlantic water is clear, rock platforms line the shore, and the area is part of a World Surfing Reserve.

entry.title: Praia da Manta Rota
entry.summary: Manta Rota is a long, wide beach on the eastern Algarve, with fine pale sand, dunes behind and shallow water that is warmer than on the west coast. A boardwalk crosses the dunes, and the village behind is small and quiet.

entry.title: Praia do Monte Clerigo
entry.summary: Monte Clerigo is a small village beach on the Atlantic coast of the Algarve near Aljezur, with a wide stretch of pale sand between rock outcrops and steep green slopes. The waves suit beginners and surfers, and at low tide the rocks form tidal pools.

entry.title: Playa de Arrietara, Sopelana
entry.summary: Playa de Arrietara is a sand beach in Sopelana on the Basque coast near Bilbao, set below tall cliffs of tilted rock layers. The Atlantic waves attract surfers, the sea is cool, and the beach is much smaller at high tide than at low tide.

entry.title: Playa de Oyambre
entry.summary: Playa de Oyambre is a long beach of golden sand in the Oyambre natural park in western Cantabria, with a river mouth, dunes and green hills behind. The Atlantic waves attract surfers, and the park has walking paths behind the shore.

entry.title: Playa de los Muertos, Carboneras
entry.summary: Playa de los Muertos is a wild beach of pale pebbles and sand near the Cabo de Gata-Nijar natural park, reached down a steep path from a car park. A tall rock stack stands at the south end, and the water is clear and deep close to the shore.

entry.title: Playa de Riazor, A Coruna
entry.summary: Riazor is the main city beach of A Coruna, a wide curve of fine sand beside the neighbouring Orzan beach and the long seafront promenade. Atlantic waves can be strong, the water is cool, and the promenade is a favourite for evening walks.

entry.title: Trstevica Beach, Prvic
entry.summary: Trstevica is a quiet pebble beach beside the village of Sepurine on Prvic, a small island in the Sibenik archipelago. The water is clear, pines give some shade, and there are no cars on the island, so the setting is peaceful.

entry.title: Valun Beach, Cres
entry.summary: Valun is a small fishing village on the west coast of Cres, with a pebble beach in a sheltered bay, old stone houses and a quiet harbour. The water is clear and calm, and the Valun Tablet, an ancient Glagolitic inscription, is kept in the village church.

entry.title: Palmizana Beach, Pakleni Islands
entry.summary: Palmizana is a bay on Sveti Klement, the largest of the Pakleni Islands off Hvar, with a pine-shaded shore of rock slabs and small pebble coves, a marina and a botanical garden. The water is clear and calm, and the bay is a popular stop for sailors.

entry.title: Lokrum Island, Dubrovnik
entry.summary: Lokrum is a small wooded island a short boat ride from the old port of Dubrovnik, with rocky shores, a botanical garden and a ruined monastery. A small salt-water lake called Mrtvo More, or the Dead Sea, has calm water for swimming, and the open sea is very clear.

entry.title: Cala Liberotto, Orosei
entry.summary: Cala Liberotto is a beach on the Orosei coast of eastern Sardinia, with fine sand and small pebbles, pine and juniper trees behind and rocks at the ends that are good for snorkelling. The sea is clear, and the shore faces east so the mornings are bright.

entry.title: Baia Verde, Gallipoli
entry.summary: Baia Verde is the beach strip south of the old town of Gallipoli in Puglia, with pale sand, patches of rock and shallow clear water. Bars, beach clubs and holiday apartments sit behind it, and the area is lively in summer with evening music.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Capriccioli
entry.summary: Capriccioli is a small beach on the Costa Smeralda in north-east Sardinia, with fine light sand, rounded granite rocks and shallow clear water. Juniper and macchia grow behind, and a rock outcrop divides the shore into two coves.

entry.title: Tonnara di Scopello
entry.summary: Tonnara di Scopello is a small cove on the north-west coast of Sicily, with an old tuna fishery building, tall sea stacks called faraglioni just offshore and very clear water. The shore is pebbles and rock, and the cove sits below a hillside of Mediterranean scrub.

entry.title: Laganas Beach, Zakynthos
entry.summary: Laganas is a long beach of fine pale sand at the head of Laganas Bay on Zakynthos, inside a national marine park where loggerhead turtles nest. The water is shallow and warm, with bars and resorts at the western end and quieter stretches towards the east.

entry.title: Kommos Beach, Crete
entry.summary: Kommos is a long beach of coarse golden sand on the south coast of Crete, close to Matala and beside the excavated site of a Minoan harbour town. The beach faces west, so the sunsets are the highlight, and waves can be strong when the wind is up.

entry.title: Aliki Beach, Thasos
entry.summary: Aliki is a small peninsula on the south-east coast of Thasos, with two sheltered bays of pale sand and clear shallow water. Pine trees grow to the shore, and ancient marble quarries and the ruins of an early Christian basilica lie behind.

entry.title: Agiofarago Beach, Crete
entry.summary: Agiofarago is a small beach at the foot of a narrow limestone gorge on the south coast of Crete, in the Heraklion region near Matala. The shore is pebbles and dark sand, the water is clear, and a small chapel stands in the gorge wall close to the sea.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Capo Coda Cavallo
entry.summary: Capo Coda Cavallo is a protected headland south of San Teodoro in north-east Sardinia, with a long curve of pale sand, red granite rocks and clear turquoise water. The area is part of a marine reserve, and the macchia scrub behind the beach is left wild.

entry.title: Sjekirica Beach, Brsecine
entry.summary: Sjekirica is a small pebble beach on the Adriatic coast north of Dubrovnik, close to the village of Brsecine, with a rocky islet just offshore and green hills behind. The water is very clear, and the beach is quiet because it is away from the main roads.

entry.title: Platja de Llafranc
entry.summary: Llafranc is a small former fishing village on the Costa Brava, with a crescent of coarse golden sand in a sheltered bay, pine-covered hills behind and a lighthouse above. The water is clear and calm, and the sea-front has restaurants and boats pulled up on the sand.

entry.title: Cala Azzurra, Favignana
entry.summary: Cala Azzurra is a small cove on the island of Favignana in the Egadi archipelago off west Sicily, with a narrow sand and pebble beach, pale rock and very clear turquoise water. The island is flat, so it is easy to cycle around, and ferries run from Trapani.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Notteri, Villasimius
entry.summary: Notteri is a long beach of fine white sand near Villasimius, on the south-east tip of Sardinia, with a coastal lagoon behind it where flamingos can sometimes be seen. The water is shallow and clear, and the sand slopes gently.
